snapshot.title: TNPSC Aptitude: Logical Reasoning & Series
snapshot.exam_hook: ⚡ TNPSC Aptitude Hook: EJOTY: 5-25. Opposite: 27. Series diff. Pythagoras: sqrt(a^2+b^2). Logic tree.

quick_notes.title: Coding-Decoding
quick_notes.detail: EJOTY (5-10-15-20-25). Opposite letters sum to 27. (e.g., A: 1, Z: 26).
quick_notes.explanation: Coding-Decoding is about finding secret rules that change letters or numbers. One useful shortcut is the EJOTY trick: the letters E, J, O, T, and Y are at positions 5, 10, 15, 20, and 25 in the alphabet, so you can quickly find the number of any letter by counting from those landmarks. Another trick is that opposite letters (the first and last, second and second-last, and so on) always add up to 27. For example, A is position 1 and Z is position 26, and 1 plus 26 equals 27; similarly, B (2) and Y (25) also sum to 27.

quick_notes.title: Number Series
quick_notes.detail: Check for: Difference, Double difference, Multiplication, Squares, Cubes, Primes.
quick_notes.explanation: A number series is a list of numbers that follow a hidden rule or pattern to get from one number to the next. To find the rule, check if the difference (the amount you add or subtract) between consecutive numbers is constant, or if the differences themselves change by a constant amount—that is called double difference. The rule might also involve multiplication (each number is multiplied by the same factor to get the next), or it could be based on squares (like 1, 4, 9, 16 which are 1 squared, 2 squared, 3 squared, 4 squared), cubes (1, 8, 27, 64), or prime numbers (like 2, 3, 5, 7, 11 which have no divisors other than 1 and themselves). Look for these simple patterns step by step, and you will uncover the rule.

quick_notes.title: Visual Reasoning
quick_notes.detail: Dice (Opposite faces), Mirror/Water Image, Completion of figures.
quick_notes.explanation: This topic helps you solve puzzles using pictures instead of words. First, Dice with Opposite Faces means that on a standard six-sided die, each face has exactly one opposite face that you cannot see at the same time; for example, if the top shows 1, the bottom must be 6, and if the front shows 2, the back must be 5, and the left and right are 3 and 4. Second, Mirror Image and Water Image are two different ways to flip a picture: a Mirror Image is like looking at yourself in a horizontal mirror, so the left side of the original becomes the right side in the reflection, while a Water Image is like looking at a picture reflected in a pool of water, so the top of the original becomes the bottom in the reflection. Third, Completion of Figures means you are given a shape that is partly missing, and you must choose the correct piece from the options to fill the empty space so the whole picture is complete and matches the pattern.

quick_notes.title: Direction Sense
quick_notes.detail: North-South-East-West. Right turn (90° clockwise). Pythagoras for shortest distance.
quick_notes.explanation: Direction Sense is a topic in logical reasoning that tests your ability to follow and visualize movement along the four cardinal directions: North, South, East, and West. A right turn means you rotate 90 degrees clockwise, so if you are facing North and take a right turn, you will face East; if facing East and take a right, you face South, and so on. When a person walks in a straight line, then turns, and walks again, the total path often forms a right-angled shape. To find the shortest distance between the starting point and the ending point, you use the Pythagorean theorem (Pythagoras), which says that in a right-angled triangle, the square of the longest side (the hypotenuse) equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides. For example, if you walk 3 km East and then 4 km North, the straight-line distance back to the start is the square root of (3 squared plus 4 squared), which is 5 km. Remember that the cardinal directions never change: North is always towards the top of a standard map, and opposite directions are 180 degrees apart.

quick_notes.title: Blood Relations
quick_notes.explanation: Blood Relations is a topic in reasoning where you map family connections using a generation tree, which is a diagram showing ancestors and descendants in order. In this tree, the plus sign (+) stands for a male person, the minus sign (-) stands for a female person, and the colon (:) indicates a married couple. For example, if you see "A + B : C - D", that means A is a male, B is a female, they are a husband and wife pair, while C is a male and D is a female, but their exact relationship to A and B depends on how the tree is drawn. You read the tree from top to bottom to identify parents and children, and from left to right to see siblings or spouses. This system helps you figure out who is whose father, mother, brother, sister, uncle, aunt, and so on.
